Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent in all the appeals.

full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J : Civil Appeal Nos. 53 and 54 of 1990 arose by leave from the judgment and order dated 12.3.90 passed by the High Court Division in FA Nos. 31 and 32 of 1989 dismissing the appeals and thereby affirming the decree dated 5.12.88 and order dated 28.1.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 350 of 1988 arising out of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988. Civil Appeal No. 55 of 1990 arose by leave from the judgment and order dated 14.3.90 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Case No. 328 of 1989 reversing the order dated 2.3.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 378 of 1988 rejecting the application filed by the defendant-appellant under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. 

 3. By Memo No. 1809/4(4) dated 2.8.78 the Government of Bangladesh in the Ministry of Communications, Roads and Highways entered into an agreement with Contractor KM Shafi Limited, a Private Limited Company (respondent in all the three appeals) for providing average 2-1/2 thick compacted premixed bituminous concrete work on the Airport Road, Dhaka. A dispute arose between the parties over payment of bill of the Contractor-respondent after completion of the work which was referred to the sole Arbitrator, namely, the Superintending Engineer, Roads and Highways. On 30.10.78 the Arbitrator gave his award. The respondent filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1979 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka under section 33 read with section 30 of the Arbitration Act for setting aside the award. It was disallowed by order dated 19.9.79. The respondent then preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 494 of 1980 in the High Court Division. By judgment and order dated 24.11.81 the High Court Division allowed the appeal in part and upheld the award in part. The High Court Division found that the Arbitrator left another dispute undecided, namely, whether the supplementary tender items claimed by the Contractor were admissible or not. The High Court Division remitted the Award to the Arbitrator to determine the unresolved dispute directing him to call for statements from both the parties, take evidence if tendered, give hearing to the parties and proceed to decide the dispute in accordance with law." 

 4. Mr. Monirul Islam succeeded Mr. Matiur Rahman as Superintending Engineer, Roads and Highways, Dhaka Roads Circle and Mr. Monirul Islam thus became the succeeding Sole Arbitrator. Seven years passed by, but the Arbitrator did not act. The respondent filed a petition of contempt of Court and the High Court Division issued a Rule which was served upon the Superintending Engineer. Then he took up the matter and passed an award for Tk. 5,59,680.02 in favour of the Contractor-respondent by Memo No. 1652 dated 27.4.88. The Contractor-respondent thereupon filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 on 13.7.88 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka under section 14/17 of the Arbitration Act for making the award a Rule of the Court. The notice was served on the appellants on 17.7.88. The appellants prayed for time thrice to file written objection on the ground, first, that papers could not be collected and secondly, that there was flood, which were allowed. On 15.9.88 the appellants prayed for time for the fourth time but the prayer was rejected on the ground that they failed to file their written objection within 30 days from service of notice on 17.7.88. The Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 was decided ex parte in favour of the respondent on 29.9.88 and the award was made a Rule of the Court. Another ex parte order was passed by the Court on 10.11.88 directing the appellants to pay the awarded amount to the Contractor by 30.11.88. By order dated 19.11.88 the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka converted the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 into Title Suit No. 350 of 1988 and accordingly a decree was drawn up making the aforesaid Award a part of the decree on 5.12.88. The appellants filed an application under section 151 CPC which was dismissed by , the learned Subordinate Judge by order dated 28.1.89. 

 7. The appellants also filed FA No. 31 of 1989 against the decree dated 5.12.88 passed in Title Suit No. 350 of 1988 converted from Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 and FA No. 32 of 1989 against the order dated 28.1.89 rejecting the appellants' application under section 151 CPC. Both the appeals have been dismissed by the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 12.3.90 out of which arise Civil Appeal Nos. 53 and 54 of 1990. 

 11. Mr. AW Bhuiyan, learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the appellants, advances several arguments in support of his submission that the Memo. in question is not an award. He submits that the Memo. was not written by Mr. Monirul Islam is his capacity as an Arbitrator. He wrote the same in his capacity as the Superintending Engineer. There is no determination of any sum payable to the Contractor and there is no direction either to pay any sum to the Contractor. The Memo.does not reveal that any arbitration proceeding was held, any witness was examined, any cross-examination took place, any documents were exhibited or any hearing took place. He submits that the Memo. was purely an inter-departmental communication addressed by the Superintending Engineer to his higher authority, namely, the Additional Chief Engineer, with a view to obtaining advance sanction for the Contractor's claimed amount in case the department has to pay the claimed amount after a regular arbitration proceeding. In fact no arbitration took place either on 27.4.88 or before or after the said date. The High Court Division, he submits, committed an illegality in dismissing the First Appeal Nos. 31 and 32 of 1989 after construing an inter-departmental letter to be an award. 

 13. The note shows that the Additional Chief Engineer directed the Superintending Engineer not to wait for any sanction. He directed immediate payment for the maintenance account and also asked the Superintending Engineer to explain why there was so much delay in the payment of award to the Contractor. This is dated 3.5.88. Mr. Ahmed then submits that a copy of the Memo. in question was forwarded to the Executive Engineer, Roads and Highways and to the Contractor-respondent who understood the Memo. in question to be an award. On the day of delivery of this judgment Mr. Ahmed has filed a copy of legal notice dated 12.6.88 served by the contractor,respondent upon the Super-intending Engineer calling upon him to pay the awarded amount of Tk. 5,59,680.02 within 7 days. A copy of the acknowledgement due receipt has also been filed showing that the legal notice was received by registered post on 15.5.88. Mr. Ahmed also submits that after filing of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 on 13.7.88 the appellants prayed for time to file written objection on three occasions but never did they raise an objection that the award was not an award within the meaning of section 2(b) of the Arbitration Act. To raise this objection no papers were necessary and the plea of flood, etc. was also untenable. He submits that the appellants raised this question for the first time in the First Appeals in the High Court Division as an after thought. 

 14. It is quite apparent from a bare reading of the Memo. in question that the Superintending Engineer was anxious to implement the High Court Division's judgment and order dated 24.11.81 passed in FMA No. 494 of 1990. All the exercises he made, namely, asking the Contractor to submit the bills and necessary papers in support of his claim in regard to supplementary tender items, asking the Executive Engineer to check up the Contractor's bills and papers and then considering both the Contractor's bills and papers and the reports of the Executive Engineer, giving a finding as to the Contractor's claim and arriving at a figure of Tk. 5,59,630.02 have been done in compliance with the order of the High Court Division. True, no formal statements were asked for from the parties, no evidence was taken and the parties were not formally heard, but the nature of exercise leaves no room for doubt that the High Court Division's order was substantially complied with. After having applied his mind to the facts of the case the Superintending Engineer came to a clear decision that the amount determined by him has to be paid to the Contractor. He was aware that there was no money sanctioned for road development in the current financial year. The Airport Road has since been transferred to Dhaka Municipal Corporation. The Contractor was pressing hard for payment of his dues and for implementing the order of the High Court Division. As such the Superintending Engineer requested the Chief Engineer to sanction the aforesaid amount to settle the matter on an urgent basis. 

 15. The learned Additional Attorney-General argues that when the Superintending Engineer wrote “বিষয়টি জরুরী ভিত্তিতে মীমাংসা করার নিমিন্ত” (to settle the matter on an urgent basis) he clearly implied that the matter was not yet arbitrated upon. He submits in support of his contention that Memo dated 27.4.88 is not an Award, that the appellants stated in paragraph 6 of Title Suit No. 378 of 1988 that the Arbitrator served a notice upon the Contractor to come for arbitration on 4.7.88, but the Contractor or his representative did not present himself on that date. The arbitration was adjourned till 9 AM of 18.7.88. A notice to that effect was not accepted by the Contractor on 6.7.88 and so the notice was sent on 7.7.88 to the Contractor by registered post. Additionally a copy of the notice was received by the learned Advocate for the Contractor. The Contractor or his representative did not attend the arbitration proceeding on 18.7.88. As the District Anti-Corruption Officer seized all the papers in this connection the appellants also could not proceed with the arbitration on 18.7.88. The Contractor filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 on 13.7.88 after receipt of the notice of arbitration dated 6.7.88. The learned Additional Attorney-General submits that all these notices were annexed in the paper book of First Appeal No. 31 of 1989, but the High Court Division failed to consider the same. 

 18. If the Memo. in question was not an award at all and if Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 was filed during the subsistence of the arbitration proceeding, then the appellants should not have taken any time to file a written objection in the matter. The proceeding of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988 could have been nipped in the bud had such a plea been taken at the earliest available opportunity. 

 24. The argument has no legs to stand. The appellants have not filed any application to set aside the award under section 17 of the Arbitration Act. Nor have they filed any application under section 33 to challenge the existence or validity of the award. It is absurd to say that by making the award a Rule of the Court, the Court has refused to set aside the award. The act of refusal must be in pursuance of a positive move by the party affected either under section 17 or under section 33. An ex parte order, as in the present case, making an award the Rule of the Court is not amenable to appeal under section 39(1) (vi) of the Arbitration Act. 

 30. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further argued that the photocopy of the award in question was filed in Court on 15.9.88 in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 63 of 1988. The award was made a Rule of the Court on 29.9.88. Under Article 158 of the Limitation Act the appellants were entitled to 30 days time from 15.9.88 to file their written objection. The award was made a Rule of the Court before the expiry of 30 days.
